title: Long-WAM: Scaling the Context of World-Action Models
why_read: A systems-and-modeling paper on giving robot control models longer visual memory in real time, with concrete deployment numbers on real hardware.
analysis: Long-WAM studies how much past visual context a robot control model needs to act well, and finds that simply having more history only helps if the underlying video model was trained in a causal, autoregressive way. Using that insight, they show success rates jumping substantially, from 63.3% to 78.7%, as context length increases on a benchmark called RoboCasa GR-1. They also engineered the system to run in real time on actual edge GPUs, reporting 107.4 milliseconds per action chunk, and demonstrated clearly superior performance on a dynamic cup-stacking task compared to other named baselines. This combination of a clear empirical insight plus real hardware deployment numbers makes it a solid applied robotics contribution.
